title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: The continuous batching scheduler has shown intermittent request starvation for low-priority/long-tail requests under high load (observed in dedicated clusters and perf canaries). This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention through priority aging, and introduce per-request timeouts and dynamic batch deadlines to protect latency SLOs. Motivation: Reduce p99 latency spikes for mixed workloads while preserving throughput and cost efficiency. Changes include algorithmic adjustments, config knobs for operational tuning, additional metrics, and end-to-end tests. Summary of changes: 1) Priority aging: requests gain priority the longer they wait, using a lightweight age-factor applied to effective priority to prevent indefinite starvation. 2) Dynamic batch deadlines: batches expose a calculated deadline based on per-request max_wait_ms and the oldest request age; this prevents long waits when a few low-latency requests block a batch. 3) Queue sharding and soft quotas: separate short/long request queues with configurable soft quotas to avoid head-of-line blocking. 4) KV cache hinting: scheduler now signals KV cache hotness for requests so the runtime can colocate or prioritize cache-friendly batches. 5) Timeouts and early flush: per-request timeout metadata allows early flush in worst-case scenarios to meet SLOs. 6) Telemetry: new metrics for queue depth by priority, age_histogram, starved_request_count, batch_deadline_misses, and requeue_rate. 7) Tests and canary plan: unit + integration tests updated; added perf canary harness configs. Backwards compatibility: default configs are safe and match previous behavior unless operators enable aggressive aging or queue sharding. Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated + hosted canaries for 48 hours, metric validation (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost), then gradual ramp to 100% with quick rollback flag. Performance results (canary): mixed latency workloads show 15-25% p99 reduction and elimination of starvation incidents in 3/3 canaries; throughput unchanged within 1-2%. Related: builds on earlier continuous-batcher scheduler tuning PRs and references ENG-5123. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests updated - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Perf canary config included - [x] Docs/runbook entry drafted - [x] Telemetry wired to metrics service - [x] Feature flagged for staged rollout. Notes: This description contains the full motivation, design summary, and rollout plan. See changed_files for implementation pointers and review_comments for discussion details.

batcher: implement dynamic batch deadline and early flush
queue: shard queues for short/long requests with soft quotas
kvcache: expose hotness hint to scheduler
metrics: add queue depth / age_histogram / starved_request_count
tests: add unit and integration tests for scheduler behaviors
docs: add runbook and tuning guide for continuous-batcher
review_comments: Evan Brooks: The priority aging factor looks good; can we bound the max effective priority to avoid priority inversion with critical background jobs?
Maya Chen: Added hard cap in scheduler.py and made it configurable via config.max_effective_priority (default=100).
Priya Nair: Can we get a flamegraph showing scheduling CPU overhead? The added computations must not increase per-token CPU significantly.
Maya Chen: Added microbenchmarks in batcher/bench and included a flamegraph in the PR artifacts. Overhead measured <2% on p99 scheduling path at 64 concurrent batches.
Lee Wong: CI initially failed on integration tests due to race around queue shutdown; please address.
Maya Chen: Fixed race by adding graceful shutdown handshake and a test that covers queue drain; reran CI.
Reviewer: Approve after small nit on config naming (max_wait_ms -> request_max_wait_ms).
Maya Chen: Renamed config and updated docs.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce request starvation and p99 latency for mixed workloads. Adds configurable priority aging, dynamic batch deadlines, queue sharding, KV cache hotness hints, and new telemetry. Backward-compatible defaults; feature flagged for staged rollout.
